title: Tech Note: Making Quick Reports Compatible with Excel
author: Yvan Ayaay, Technical Support Engineer, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: QR SET HTML TEMPLATE / QR SET DESTINATION commands
Custom XML schemas for Microsoft Excel 2003

historical_commentary.text: This note shows how to hijack 4D's Quick Report HTML-templating tags to generate XML output (both a generic custom XML schema and Excel's own SpreadsheetML/XML Spreadsheet format) that Microsoft Excel 2003 could open directly. It is a clever but very version-specific workaround from an era before 4D had first-class Excel/spreadsheet export commands and long before modern file formats like .xlsx (OOXML) existed. While the specific Excel 2003 XML Spreadsheet schema and Quick Report tag-based templating approach are now obsolete, the underlying idea of programmatically generating structured export files for spreadsheet consumption is still a relevant integration pattern.
related_updates: Microsoft Excel moved to the .xlsx (Office Open XML) format starting with Excel 2007, superseding the XML Spreadsheet (SpreadsheetML) format targeted by this note
4D has since added more direct commands and libraries for generating modern spreadsheet files, reducing the need for this HTML-template-tag workaround
